why: Mapping raw forge JSON to yan's closed return sets is the part of lib-forge.sh most likely to be wrong in production, so it is tested against payloads that really came off the wire - not against shapes someone remembered. Every file below says where it came from and whether it was verified against a live server. Read `verified: false` as 'nobody has ever seen a server send exactly this'.

github/mr-merged-mergecommit.json.note: This repository's own PR #1, landed with a merge commit. Read-only call.

github/mr-merged-squash-branch-deleted.j.note: Squash-merged: mergeCommit 62efc15 differs from headRefOid e4b4931, so the head commit is NOT an ancestor of the base branch. The head branch williammartin-scaling-guacamole has also been deleted (branches API returns 404). Both awkward cases in one payload; the forge still says MERGED.

github/mr-closed-unmerged.json.note: Closed without merging, and a draft, so it also proves isDraft does not affect the state mapping.

github/mr-api-error.stdout.txt.note: Empty. This is what the mapper is handed when the forge refuses; it must answer unknown, not crash.

github/ci-none.json.note: Empty rollup - this repository runs no CI. Maps to none.

github/ci-checks-green.json.note: Checks API only. First six entries of the real rollup, each object copied verbatim; the rest were dropped so the fixture stays readable. SUCCESS plus SKIPPED.

github/ci-checks-mixed-red.json.note: Two real FAILURE CheckRuns, two SUCCESS and one SKIPPED, each object verbatim, selected from a much larger real rollup. Any failure means red.

github/ci-checks-running.json.note: Three IN_PROGRESS CheckRuns (note conclusion is the empty string, not null) plus two SUCCESS, objects verbatim, selected from a larger rollup.

github/ci-status-green.json.note: Legacy commit-status API only (StatusContext, from node's Jenkins). Four verbatim objects selected from a larger rollup.

github/ci-status-pending.json.note: Two PENDING StatusContexts mixed with two SUCCESS CheckRuns - both GitHub CI systems in one array. Objects verbatim, selected from a larger rollup.

github/ci-status-red.json.note: Legacy StatusContexts, two FAILURE and two SUCCESS. Objects verbatim, selected from a larger rollup.

github/ci-red-beats-pending.json.note: A real rollup that is failing while other jobs are still running. Objects verbatim, selected from a larger rollup. Pins the precedence rule: red beats pending.

gitlab/mr-merged.json.note: DOCUMENTATION-DERIVED, NOT CAPTURED. No GitLab account was available, so no glab call was ever made against a live server. Field names and value vocabularies (state, merged_at, head_pipeline.status) come from the published API documentation; ids, hostnames and shas are invented.

gitlab/mr-locked.json.source: GitLab REST API documentation - merge request state is one of opened, closed, locked, merged
gitlab/mr-locked.json.note: DOCUMENTATION-DERIVED, NOT CAPTURED. `locked` is the fourth GitLab state; yan collapses it onto open.

gitlab/mr-state-unknown-to-yan.json.note: SYNTHETIC. A state GitLab does not currently document, to prove an unrecognised value becomes unknown rather than leaking through.

gitlab/ci-failed.json.source: GitLab pipeline status vocabulary: created, waiting_for_resource, preparing, pending, running, success, failed, canceled, skipped, manual, scheduled

gitlab/ci-no-pipeline.json.source: GitLab REST API documentation - head_pipeline is null when no pipeline ran

gitlab/ci-legacy-pipeline-field.json.source: GitLab REST API documentation - older servers expose `pipeline` rather than `head_pipeline`
